run.rulesInOwnWords:
Six teams in a line (1 = entry, 6 = customer end), each with a WIP limit, an upper mark and a lower mark; all start ROUTINE, closed tally starts at 0. Each sprint runs five steps, each step finished for all teams before the next:
1. Arrivals: add that sprint's New Tickets amount to every team. No WIP cap here.
2. Overflow: go team 1, 2, ..., 6 in order. If a team holds more than its WIP limit, cut it to the limit and pass the excess to the next team (which is handled afterwards, so the excess can cascade). Team 6's excess is closed and added to the closed tally.
3. Status: using post-step-2 counts, ROUTINE with count >= upper mark becomes ESCALATED; ESCALATED with count <= lower mark becomes ROUTINE; otherwise unchanged. At most one change per team per sprint; log each change.
4. Work-off: from the counts at the start of this step, compute every team's amount first (ROUTINE: floor(count/4); ESCALATED: floor(count/2)). Then apply simultaneously: each team loses its amount; ROUTINE amounts are closed (tally); ESCALATED amounts are bounced to the previous team (team 1's ESCALATED amount is closed instead). Bounced-in tickets do not change already computed amounts. No WIP cap here.
5. Halving: if the six-team total is strictly more than 38, every team's count becomes floor(count/2) and the removed tickets are added to the closed tally; record the sprint. A total of exactly 38 does not fire.
After sprint 5 step 5, report. Balance: starting total + all arrivals = end total + closed tally.
